what: EdgeGuard connected to a self-hosted MEC Sandbox (AdvantEDGE v1.9.2, the open-source base of the ETSI MEC Sandbox) running our own warehouse scenario
host: team desktop (Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32 GB, Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC): Hyper-V VM Ubuntu 22.04, 6 vCPU / 16 GB, Kubernetes 1.27; EdgeGuard stack on Docker Desktop of the same PC
scenario: scenarios/edgeguard-warehouse.json (2 forklifts, 4 workers, 2 private-5G cells, MEC edge); MOVEMENT, MOBILITY, POAS-IN-RANGE automation on
path: AdvantEDGE Location API (/edgeguard/location/v2) -> MEC-IPE -> Mobius IN-CSE resources -> subscription -> EdgeGuard MEC app -> alerts
install_notes: k8s v1.27 apt repo key expired -> repository trusted explicitly
Helm 3.7 snap channel gone -> binary from get.helm.sh
Debian 11 left the mirrors -> auth-svc / virt-engine / tc-sidecar images built on debian:12-slim
Bitnami images moved -> bitnamilegacy plain tags, minideb bookworm; kube-state-metrics from registry.k8s.io
platform auth subrequest returned 500 -> auth disabled (single-team lab host)
scenario needed deployment.connectivity / d2d for the 1.9 validator
notes: This run classified forklift_02 (10.100.0.12) as a worker: one 4 s speed sample caught it slowing (0.75 m/s), so 5 pairs instead of 8. sandbox_probe now classifies by peak speed over 12 s (verified against the scenario replay: 2 forklifts, 4 workers) and accepts --forklifts.
No RNIS cell load in this scenario run (ipe_cell_containers 0) - the congestion margin stayed off.
